question:
Which HCs are demonstrated in this project? Tie each suggestion to something I actually did.

I am writing a recommendation about the campus shuttle timetable. We collected comments from students who ride the shuttle at different times of day. Some comments described missed connections while others described empty seats. My introduction describes the service and explains why the timetable matters to students. It also describes the stops and the difference between weekday and weekend travel. These details establish the setting for the recommendation. I recorded them separately from the analysis so that I could tell which statements were background and which statements supported a decision.

Before using external information, I inspected the credentials of the authors of several transport reports, checked how recently the reports were updated, and looked for an explanation of how their numbers had been verified. I compared an operator's promotional page with an independently published report. I noted who funded each report and what each publisher might gain from a favorable conclusion. Where an article summarized another study, I located the original study to see whether its limits and qualifications had been preserved. I documented the reasons for trusting each source rather than relying on how professional its website looked.

Our working document also records mundane project details. It lists the places we met, which draft each person edited, and when we expect to give the presentation. We exchanged some notes about formatting and agreed on the labels to use for the stops. Those details helped coordinate the project, but I would not present them as evidence for the proposed timetable. The analysis section explains how the observations connect to the decisions. Several sentences still need editing, and I have not yet settled on the final wording of the recommendation.

The final section reports an estimate of mean waiting time using a random sample of journeys. I calculated a confidence interval with lower and upper bounds and explained what the interval says about precision. I described the confidence level in terms of the coverage of intervals under repeated sampling. I considered how the recommendation would change if the estimate were near either endpoint, rather than treating the sample mean as an exact description of every student's experience. I also explained why greater variability would make a wider range of plausible population values important when discussing the results.

gold_evidence.anchor_quote: Sources of information can be scrutinized in terms of their currency, relevance, authority, accuracy, and purpose.
A confidence interval specifies upper and lower values that are likely to bracket an unknown population value—typically the true mean of the population.

must_include: Connect sourcequality to the report checks and confidenceintervals to the final analysis.
must_not_claim: Assign an official grade or claim that unseen work has been verified.
